question: Metabolic syndrome in the Indian context requires the presence of central obesity (waist ≥90 cm men / ≥80 cm women) as a mandatory component, along with at least two of: raised triglycerides, low HDL, raised blood pressure, or raised fasting glucose.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The IDF criteria for South Asians mandate central obesity (waist ≥90 cm in men, ≥80 cm in women) and at least two of: triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, HDL <40 mg/dL (men)/<50 mg/dL (women), BP ≥130/85, or fasting glucose ≥100 mg/dL.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Using IDF/modified NCEP-ATP III criteria for South Asians, central obesity is the mandatory anchor with ethnicity-specific waist thresholds (men ≥90 cm, women ≥80 cm), plus ≥2 of the remaining four metabolic criteria.
